timeline.body:
It seems the best way to fix https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/122949 is to use existing data stream [reindex API](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/master/data-stream-reindex-api.html). However, this API is located in the `migrate` x-pack plugin. This commit moves the system indices migration logic (REST handlers, transport actions, and task) to the `migrate` plugin.

There will be a separate PR to add system data streams migration, as well as additional PRs for main/9.0, since these changes can't be automatically backported from main to 8.x.

timeline.body: The only notable change in logic in this PR is that we now use CreateIndexAction to create a new system index for migration. Because of this, I had to add a workaround to allow the creation of such an index with the correct name specifically for migration purposes.
We don't have access to MetadataCreateIndexService from the persistent task in the plugin

timeline.body: Does this actually indicate that the migration is in progress?  If this index exists, doesn't this only show that the migration has at some point started (and perhaps even completed)? Or, is it not possible to get to this point if the migraiton has already completed?

reply.body:
This is a transport action that creates an index. So, if there's a request to create an index with the `SystemIndices.UPGRADED_INDEX_SUFFIX` suffix, it means something has triggered it. The idea here is that this request has been sent by SystemIndexMigrator when attempting to reindex an existing index for a new version.
There's still a possibility that someone could manually try to create an index with that suffix. In that case, it would be allowed and treated as a system index, but I don’t think that’s likely. I'll take a look at how we can prevent that scenario

timeline.body: Can you help me understand when this codepath is executed?  I'm a bit unsure of the context that motivates the changes in this function.  Why do we now differentiate if `indexMigrationInProgress`, and then update the mappings/settings/indexName differently for each branch of execution?

reply.body: The other branch is executed when the request comes from an external system (e.g. Kibana), where we ignore settings/mappings/aliases/index name from the request, instead taking them from the index descriptor. Here, when the request is part of a system index migration, it includes settings and mappings specifically created by `SystemIndexMigrator` for that process, so we use them. (I doubt there's any difference in real world, but some tests rely on this behavior). Additionally, we don't create an alias in this case because it already exists, pointing to the current index, and SystemIndexMigrator will handle it later. Finally, regarding the index name – an index with `descriptor.getPrimaryIndex()` already exists, and we need to create a new index with the name `descriptor.getPrimaryIndex() + SystemIndices.UPGRADED_INDEX_SUFFIX` and this is the name from the request.

We didn't need this logic before, because we were bypassing it using MetadataCreateIndexService directly, but it is not available from plugins without introducing another transport message, which is probably too much for now

Will this will still work when _creating_ a new managed/unmanged system index?  Asking since the paths you described are:
a) migration happening for managed system index
b) migration happening for externally managed system index
Will a request for a brand new system index (or a move to a system index) hit the same logic?

No reason to to think it won't be (since tests are passing), but thought it best to check with you to be sure.

This branch is under the `if (indexMigrationInProgress)` check, so it shouldn’t be executed for a completely new index. The condition `boolean indexMigrationInProgress = cause.equals(SystemIndices.MIGRATE_SYSTEM_INDEX_CAUSE) && request.index().endsWith(SystemIndices.UPGRADED_INDEX_SUFFIX)` ensures that the request is part of migration. The `cause` value, as I understand it, can't be set via REST API, and the only place in the codebase where it's set to `SystemIndices.MIGRATE_SYSTEM_INDEX_CAUSE` is in `SystemIndexMigrator`. Therefore, any request hitting this logic is coming from migration process and not from the creation of a new system index.

Move of an existing index to a system index doesn't execute this code - it is just a metadata update of the index: `org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService`. System index mappings update also doesn't involve reindexing: `org.elasticsearch.indices.SystemIndexMappingUpdateService`

If there's a real problem with index creation, the stack trace will still appear as a suppressed exception in the following errors. At least, that's how it worked for me while debugging this code:)
